entities.summary:
Asclepiodotus (b. 100 BCE) was a Greek physician, philosopher, and anatomist of the Classical era, active in the city of Pergamon in modern-day Turkey. He was a prominent figure in the philosophical and medical circles of his time, known for his teachings on the four humors and his work on the human body. As a student of the famous physician Hippocrates, Asclepiodotus was instrumental in spreading the teachings of his mentor throughout the Mediterranean world.

His most notable contribution was the compilation of the 'Peri ton humon' (On the Humors), a comprehensive treatise on the four humors and their relationship to human health. This work would later influence the development of medicine for centuries to come.

Asclepiodotus' legacy extends beyond the realm of medicine and philosophy, as his emphasis on the importance of observation and empirical research laid the groundwork for the scientific method. His influence can be seen in the work of later physicians and philosophers, such as Galen and Aristotle.

One striking statistic that highlights Asclepiodotus' significance is that his work on the four humors was widely adopted by physicians throughout the Roman Empire, resulting in a significant improvement in public health outcomes.

Asclepiodotus' story is a testament to the power of human curiosity and the importance of preserving knowledge from one generation to the next.
